title: Senior's toolkit: errors you can diagnose
summary: Break when thrown, full exception logging, guard helpers, structured logs and testable time.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: errors you can diagnose
steps.body: Robust code fails early, fails loudly, and leaves enough behind to find the cause from a log line at 3 a.m. These are the APIs and debugger settings that make that possible.

toolkit.what: Stop at the exact `throw`, before any `catch` runs, with every variable still there.
flags: Ctrl+Alt+E, tick the exception type under Common Language Runtime Exceptions
Breakpoints section > All Exceptions or User-Unhandled Exceptions
tick only `System.NullReferenceException` to avoid stopping on expected ones
toolkit.example: Ctrl+Alt+E, search NullReference, tick it, F5

toolkit.what: Log the exception object itself, plus a message template with named placeholders. You get the type, message, stack trace and every inner exception, and `FileName` becomes a searchable field.
flags: the exception is the first argument, not part of the text
a named hole: stored as a property, not just pasted into text
an interpolated string loses the fields and is built even when the level is off

toolkit.what: When you must print an exception, print `ToString()`: it contains the type, the message, the stack trace and the whole `InnerException` chain. `ex.Message` alone throws all of that away.
flags: the original cause, wrapped by a higher-level exception
--- End of inner exception stack trace ---
the line that separates the layers in the output

toolkit.what: Rethrow the caught exception with its original stack trace. `throw ex;` resets the trace to the current line and hides where it really happened.
flags: wrap with context, keep the cause as InnerException
avoid: loses the original location (analyzer CA2200)

toolkit.what: One-line guard clauses with the parameter name filled in for you.
Ask an injected `TimeProvider` for the time instead of `DateTime.Now`, so tests can control the clock. Tests use `FakeTimeProvider` from the Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing package.
flags: the current time as a `DateTimeOffset` in UTC

toolkit.cmd: int.TryParse(text, NumberStyles.Integer, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var n)
toolkit.what: Parse input without exceptions and without depending on the machine's language settings. A server in Germany reads `1,5` differently from one in the US.
flags: returns false instead of throwing FormatException
fixed rules for files, config and APIs
toolkit.example:
if (!decimal.TryParse(cell, NumberStyles.Number, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var amount))
    errors.Add($"Row {row}: '{cell}' is not a number");

steps.prompt: Production logs only show this line, many times a day. Nobody can tell where it comes from. What is the fix in the logging code?
steps.code: ERROR Order failed: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
options: It logs `ex.Message`; log the exception object (`logger.LogError(ex, "Order {OrderId} failed", id)`) so the stack trace and inner exceptions are kept
Lower the log level to Debug
Add more `Console.WriteLine` calls around the order code
steps.explain: The message of a `NullReferenceException` never says which reference. The stack trace says which method and line, and it is only there if the exception itself is logged.

code: throw new InvalidOperationException("Bad config value 'Port'", ex);
steps.explain: `finally` runs before the exception leaves the inner `try`. The wrapper says what was being done; its `InnerException` keeps the real cause.

steps.prompt: Match each line to what it does.
pairs: rethrows and keeps the original stack trace
rethrows but the trace starts here
adds context and keeps the cause
a guard with the parameter name filled in
logs the full exception with a template

steps.prompt: Log the failure so `OrderId` is a searchable field and the stack trace is kept.
steps.explain: The exception goes first so it is logged whole. A named placeholder becomes a property you can filter on (`OrderId = 1042`); `{0}` works but gives the field a useless name.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Every `catch` either handles the problem or adds context and rethrows with the cause attached; none of them logs `ex.Message` alone. Guard public methods with the `ThrowIf...` helpers, inject `TimeProvider` wherever time matters, and switch on break-when-thrown the moment a stack trace does not point to the real line.
